summary:
Per-bank counts: Goldman 3, Apollo/Slok 1, Deutsche 1 (5 items, 3 banks/strategists).

Goldman spans macro data: a Core Retail Sales beat lifting the Q3 GDP tracking estimate to +3.0%, a decomposition of the labor share decline into pass-through entities/depreciation/equity comp, and an Empire Manufacturing miss with rising prices-paid components.

Torsten Slok (Apollo) argues hyperscaler CDS widening reflects a repricing of deteriorating credit fundamentals — debt-financed AI capex, rising leverage, negative FCF — not dealer hedging.

Deutsche Bank's historical framework (via @johnauthers) flags that once Fed tightening starts it tends to persist, with the 10-year yield potentially testing 6% before the cycle ends.

No @neilksethi/@neilksethinew tweets appeared in this collection window. All 5 items were sourced same-day or prior-day via relay accounts MikeZaccardi (4) and dailychartbook (1); no cross-account duplicates found.

items.text:
GS: 40% of the labor share decline isn't a shift from labor to capital 📉📊

It's:
1️⃣ Pass-through entities: Tax incentives moved wage income into business profits 🏢
2️⃣ Depreciation: More tech/software means faster capital wear-and-tear 💻
3️⃣ Equity comp 📈 https://t.co/cxBHxvn2D0

banks.theme: Hyperscaler CDS widening reflects AI-capex credit risk, not dealer hedging (Torsten Slok)

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
Hyperscaler CDS widening isn't dealer hedging... otherwise, bank spreads would be moving too 📉. 

Instead, the market is repricing deteriorating credit fundamentals: debt-financed AI capex, rising leverage, and negative FCF with uncertain ROI 🤖💸.

Torsten at Apollo https://t.co/20qAPzC8Re

banks.theme: Historical Fed tightening cycles point to a 10-year yield test of 6% (via @johnauthers)

items.author: dailychartbook
items.text:
Once the Fed embarks on tightening, it generally continues for a while, and yields continue to rise, generally by more than a percentage point. Judging by history ... we should brace for the 10-year yield to reach 6% before the Fed is done."

Deutsche Bank via @johnauthers https://t.co/0TRh3ZkU0Y
